page.layout: One page of text in a single main column; a narrow strip of text at the right edge of the scan belongs to the facing page and is cut off mid-word, so it is a margin of the neighbouring page and is transcribed as notes only where clearly legible. Page number at the head centred.

main_text.p: rum irritamenta, &, uno nomine, instrumentum est omnis nequitiæ) possit magnam illius partem citissimè ad has & illas terræ partes amandare, illaque mediante innumera tam in terræ viscceribus, quàm in ejus superficie producere.
main_text.head: V.
main_text.p: Firmiter tamen statui posse videtur malum Genium mente nostra in hoc inferiorem esse, quòd non pro lubitu & quoties vult per hæc corpora agere possit, uti mens nostro si modò illud sit bene dispositum. Nam ex jam dictis patet, quòd talis nexus naturalis inter quodcunque corpus, & inter malum Genium non sit, adeoque se toties solum eis jungere queat, quoties Deus hoc aut jubet eoque utitur, vel tanquam carnifice suo & exequutore voluntatis & justitiæ suæ ut homines cruciet, seu quoad corpus solùm, seu quoad mentem solam, seu quoad utrumque, vel tanquam instrumento quodam, quo fides hominum, ejusque constantia probatur, aut in quemcunque tandem finem hanc conjunctionem ipsi permittit. Si enim toties, quoties ipsi liberet, uti corporibus possfet, ad suam voluntatem exequendam, nunquam non abutcretur, imò exiguo tempore omnia

page.notes: Left and right margins contain fragments of the facing page (partial lines such as "omn", "tam", "lian", "mir", "tue", "per", "qu", "tur", "ext", "pla", "ref" at the right edge) which are cut off and not transcribed. Several words in the scan are blurred, notably "statui posse" and "possfet", and "Genium" in the text may be "Genium" as printed; these are read as printed with low certainty.
